newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians throng Arafat in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians throng Arafat in Hebron.

text.p: Tens of thousands of Palestinians greeted Yasser Arafat in Hebron on Sunday, giving a hero's welcome to the Palestinian president who was visiting the town for the first time since it came under self-rule.
Schoolchildren and notables from nearby villages headed towards Hebron from dawn, many on foot, while boy scouts carrying Palestinian flags and singing national songs marched through the streets.

"We are very happy to see Arafat in Hebron. We never imagined the Israelis ever leaving the city, but we had hoped Arafat would make the settlers leave," said Sarhan Taradi, 28, a construction worker.

There were no official estimates but reporters said about 25,000 people from Hebron and nearby villages cheered and waved as the Palestinian leader's helicopters flew over the town. Officials had forecast a crowd half that size.
Arafat's security guards, fearing he would be crushed by the crowds, rushed him into his bullet-proof car as soon as his helicopter landed.
To the surprise and unease of his security, Arafat shook hands with people who thrust themselves at the car. Police pushed other well-wishers away.

"It was impossible for Arafat to review the guard of honour when we saw the thousands of people rushing towards him. The police could not control the crowds, and we were afraid he would be crushed," a PLO official said.
"But it was a pleasant surprise because we didn't expect that many people to show up," the official said.

Hebronites have a reputation for switching loyalties. They were the first Palestinians to ask King Hussein to unite the West Bank with Jordan in 1951. Palestinians in other cities objected to the union and stood by demands for independence.

Although Hebronites rejoiced at the redeployment of Israeli troops from 80 percent of the city, many said they were frustrated the heart of the city remained under Israeli occupation for the protection of 400 militant Jewish settlers.

Israel pulled its troops out of most of the city at dawn on Friday. Hebronites decorated the "liberated" part of Hebron with Palestinian flags, Arafat posters and banners welcoming the Palestinian Authority to the city.
"We have waited for you too long," said a banner carried by children at al-Amara, the former Israeli prison and military headquarters, which has now become the PLO's security headquarters.
Hebronites have bad memories of al-Amara's cells, where many men have been jailed. Hebronites crowded the al-Amara grounds to greet Arafat and tell stories of their imprisonments.
Atef Balas, 21, a member of Arafat's police force, said he was among the first to enter al-Amara after Israel pulled out.

"I was imprisoned here for six months. I kissed the walls of the cell I was jailed in because finally I entered this building as a liberated man. I can't find words to express my happiness," Balas told Reuters.
Women ululated as Arafat said: "Oh my dear beloved brave Hebronites, you are the heroes."
